verdict.rationale: Stagehand's own docs say it caches act(), observe() and extract() results to reduce LLM costs and speed up automations. A dedicated guide describes auto-caching that turns agent-discovered workflows into deterministic scripts running 10-100x faster, and recorded selectors are replayed, with selfHeal re-inferring only when one breaks. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of cache replay savings, and detailed documentation of cache configuration and invalidation (the evidence is short snippets, with the deterministic-script guide on v3 docs).

support.subject: As a developer, I can cache resolved actions or generated code so repeat runs replay deterministically at lower cost and latency than re-prompting the LLM

citations.quote: Stagehand caches `act()`, `observe()`, and `extract()` results server-side to reduce LLM costs and speed up your automations.
use Stagehand's built-in auto-caching to convert agent-discovered workflows into fast, deterministic scripts that run 10-100x faster
Turn on `selfHeal` to re-infer an action when its recorded selector breaks.
